subject: MSA + Order Form: damage categorization & liability language — ACME
body:
From: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps Team <legalops@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MSA redlines + Order Form (liability/damages)

Connor — attaching our redline of the MSA and the latest Order Form (v3). We flagged the limitation of liability and damages sections. High level: ACME cannot accept broad exclusions for lost profits and loss of data given our regulated customers; we need carve-outs for data loss and certain security incidents. We also propose that lost profits (where directly caused by a Redwood outage) be recoverable as direct damages in defined scenarios.

Please see attached: ACME_MSA_redline.pdf, OrderForm_ACME_v3.xlsx. We marked our must-haves in red and our preferences in yellow.

Summary of our positions (top priorities):
- Carve out data-loss remediation costs and documented lost profits for material incidents (we propose metric-based thresholds).
- Exclude only the typical "consequential/indirect" damages like third-party claims and speculative business impacts.
- We need clearer definitions for "direct" v. "indirect" damages with examples.

Happy to discuss next week — can you loop in your legal?

[Attachment: ACME_MSA_redline.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)]
[Attachment: OrderForm_ACME_v3.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)]

Best,
James Park
Head of Procurement

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines + Order Form (liability/damages)

James — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Looping in Neha (Legal) and Lauren (Sales Lead) to recommend language and a negotiation stance.

Quick thoughts from GTM: we want to move fast on this deal but also protect platform economics. Our usual position is:
- Overall liability cap equal to greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $1M (mutual).
- Carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and breach of confidentiality/data protection (we typically try to keep these uncapped or subject to a separate sub-cap).
- Define "direct damages" to include reasonable costs to restore data and reasonable, documented lost profits where causation is proven.

Can you prioritize your top three non-negotiables (e.g., uncapped for data loss; lost profits always recoverable; removal of fees-based cap entirely)? That will help us prepare a focused counter. Also propose 30-min call windows Mon/Tue next week.

I'll review Neha's language once she sends it.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, James Park <james.park@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ACME MSA redlines + Order Form (liability/damages)

Connor / Team / James — attaching a short set of clause alternatives and an annotated draft I recommend we propose. Key points and proposed drafting: see attachments annotated_clauses.docx and examples_direct_vs_indirect_snippets.txt.

Proposed drafting (high level) — pick A or B in negotiations:

1) Definition of Direct vs Indirect Damages (example language):
"Direct Damages" means money damages that arise directly and solely from a party's breach of this Agreement and that are actually and reasonably incurred. Examples: (a) reasonable costs to restore or reproduce lost data; (b) reasonable, documented lost profits directly resulting from Redwood's failure to deliver Services as specified in an applicable Order Form; and (c) amounts payable to third parties to remediate a breach of Customer Data.

"Indirect, Special, Consequential or Incidental Damages" means damages that do not arise directly from a breach and include, without limitation, lost business, lost goodwill, loss of use, loss of revenue not documented by contemporaneous evidence, and punitive damages.

2) Liability Cap (our recommended starting point):
Option A (standard): Each party's aggregate liability for Direct Damages shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form giving rise to the claim in the 12 months preceding the claim; or (ii) US$1,000,000.
Option B (compromise for regulated customers): For claims arising from unauthorized access to or loss of Customer Data, the aggregate liability shall be subject to a sub-cap of US$250,000 for data restoration and related remediation costs, and such claims shall otherwise be subject to the general cap.

3) Carve-outs (negotiable):
- Liability for each party's gross negligence or willful misconduct (uncapped).
- Liability for breaches of confidentiality or Customer Data (we recommend either uncapped or a specific sub-cap as in Option B above).
- IP infringement (typically uncapped).

4) Example clause for Order Form (short, implementable):
"Notwithstanding the limitation of liability in Section X of the MSA, for the purposes of this Order Form, 'Direct Damages' shall include reasonable and documented costs to restore Customer Data and reasonable lost profits directly caused by Redwood's failure to provide Services in accordance with the applicable Service Level Agreement, provided that Customer's recovery for such items shall not exceed the greater of (i) fees paid under this Order Form in the prior 12 months, or (ii) US$250,000, except to the extent recoverable under applicable law for willful misconduct or IP infringement."

Notes on lost profits: we will push for strict causation language and contemporaneous evidence (sales forecasts, PO cancellations) and a cap tied to fees or a fixed sub-cap. This reduces speculative claims while preserving ACME's ability to recover for concrete business harm.

I'll attach annotated_clauses.docx with inline edits and the examples file for sample fact patterns. Happy to jump on a call to walk through.

[Attachment: annotated_clauses.docx (DOCX, 12 KB)]
[Attachment: examples_direct_vs_indirect_snippets.txt (TXT, 4 KB)]

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, James Park <james.park@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ACME MSA redlines + Order Form (liability/damages)

Team — quick alignment from Sales/AM: we can accept Neha's drafting approach. Practical guidance for the negotiation:

- Aim for mutual cap = greater of 12 months' fees or $1M.
- For data restoration, push to clarify scope (reasonable remediation costs, forensics, notification). I'm comfortable with a specific sub-cap for data restoration costs at $250k rather than leaving it wholly uncapped — that is an easier sell to Procurement.
- Reserve unlimited liability only for willful misconduct and statutory obligations (e.g., data protection law where uncapped liability may apply).

Connor: please propose these three items in our counter and ask ACME which of their redline priorities are absolute musts vs preferences. Schedule a 30-min call; my calendar has Mon 11–12 or Tue 14–16 PT.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Sales — Enterprise

From: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines + Order Form (liability/damages)

Connor / Neha / Lauren — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear options. ACME's updated stance after internal review:

- We can consider a fees-based cap for most claims, but we need retained ability to recover lost profits in cases where the incident directly interrupts our revenue stream from named customers (we will provide contemporaneous evidence).
- We prefer the data restoration carve-out to cover both (i) costs to restore/restore data and (ii) verified lost profits that directly flow from that data loss, with a sub-cap not below $500,000 for regulated workloads.
- If Redwood insists on $250k for data remediation, we will push back strongly — $500k is our minimum for regulated customers.

Next steps from ACME: please incorporate Neha's baseline language into a counter-redline and highlight the two options (A: standard cap; B: regulated customer sub-cap + $500k data remediation) so our counsel can review. We'll book a 30-min call after we see the updated redline.

Also please include a short illustrative example in the Order Form appendix (one paragraph) showing how lost profits would be calculated in a direct-damage scenario — that will help our finance team.

Thanks — look forward to the counter.

James Park
Head of Procurement
ACME Corporation
[Preferred contact: +1 415 555 0199]

----

Thread notes: Connor to produce a counter-redline that (a) includes Neha's Option A and Option B language, (b) proposes mutual cap = greater of 12 months' fees or $1M, (c) proposes $250k sub-cap for data remediation as Redwood's opening compromise with an option to escalate to $500k for regulated workloads if required, and (d) prepare a one-paragraph illustrative calculation for the Order Form appendix.
